word_for_word: किंच -- ज्योतिषामिति। ज्योतिषां चन्द्रादित्यादीनामपि तज्ज्योतिः प्रकाशकं ततोयेन सूर्यस्तपति तेजसेद्धःन तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः। तमेव भान्तमनु भाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति इत्यादिश्रुतेः। अतएव तमसोऽज्ञानात्परं तेनासंस्पृष्टमुच्यते।आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् इत्यादिश्रुतेः। ज्ञानं च तदेव बुद्धिवृत्तावभिव्यक्तं? तदेव रूपाद्याकारेण ज्ञेयं च ज्ञानेन गम्यं चअमानित्वमदम्भित्वम् इत्यादिलक्षणेन पूर्वोक्तेन ज्ञानसाधनेन प्राप्यमित्यर्थः। ज्ञानगम्यं विशिनष्टि। सर्वस्य प्राणिमात्रस्य हृदि विष्ठितं विशेषेणाप्रच्युतस्वरूपेण नियन्तृतया स्थितम्। धिष्ठितमिति पाठेऽधिष्ठाय स्थितमित्यर्थः।

Further, it is the light even of lights such as the moon and sun, their illuminator. Scripture says, ‘By whose brilliance the sun shines,’ and ‘There the sun does not shine, nor moon and stars, nor these lightnings—how then this fire? Everything shines after that shining One; by its light all this shines.’ Therefore it is said to be beyond darkness, ignorance, untouched by it, as in ‘sun-colored, beyond darkness.’ It itself, manifested in the modification of intellect, is knowledge; it itself, appearing as forms and other objects, is what is known; and it is reached by knowledge—that is, by the previously described means to knowledge beginning with humility and absence of hypocrisy. He qualifies ‘reachable by knowledge’: it is specially established in the heart of every living being, remaining as the unfailing inner ruler. If the reading is ‘adhiṣṭhitam,’ it means ‘remaining having presided over.’

उक्तं क्षेत्रादिकमधिकारिफलसहितमुपसंहरति -- इतीति। इत्येवं क्षेत्रं महाभूतादिधृत्यन्तं तथा ज्ञानं च अमानित्वादितत्त्वज्ञानार्थदर्शनान्तम्। ज्ञेयं चअनादिमत्पर ब्रह्म इत्यादिविष्ठितम् इत्यन्तम्। वसिष्ठादिभिर्विस्तरेणोक्तं सर्वमपि मया संक्षेपेणोक्तम्। एतच्च पूर्वाध्यायोक्तलक्षणो मद्भक्तो विज्ञाय मद्भावाय ब्रह्मत्वायोपपद्यते योग्यो भवति।

He concludes the field and the rest together with the qualification of the aspirant and the fruit. Thus the field has been stated from the great elements through firmness; knowledge from humility through seeing the purpose of truth-knowledge; and the knowable from ‘beginningless Supreme Brahman’ through ‘established in the heart.’ Everything taught at length by Vasiṣṭha and others has been stated by Me briefly. A devotee of Mine possessing the qualities described in the previous chapter, knowing this, becomes fit for My state, for Brahmanhood.

तदेवंतत्क्षेत्रं यच्च यादृक्च इत्येतावत्प्रपञ्चितम्। इदानीं तुयद्विकारि यतश्च यत्। स च यो यत्प्रभावश्च इत्येतत्पूर्वं प्रतिज्ञातमेव प्रकृतिपुरुषयोः संसारहेतुत्वकथनेन प्रपञ्चयति -- प्रकृतिमिति पञ्चभिः। तत्र प्रकृतिपुरुषयोरादिमत्त्वे तयोरपि प्रकृत्यन्तरेण भाव्यमित्यनवस्थापत्तिः स्यात्। अतस्तावुभावनादी विद्धि। अनादेरीश्वरस्य शक्तित्वात्प्रकृतिरनादिः? पुरुषोऽपि तदंशत्वादनादिरेव? अत्र च परमेश्वरस्य तच्छक्तीनां चानादित्वं नित्यत्वं च श्रीमच्छंकरभगवद्भाष्यकृद्भिरतिप्रबन्धेनोपपादितमिति ग्रन्थबाहुल्यान्नास्माभिः प्रतन्यते। विकारांश्च देहेन्द्रियादीन्? गुणांश्च गुणपरिणामान्सुखदुःखमोहादीन्प्रकृतेः संभवान्संभूतान्विद्धि।

Thus ‘what the field is and what it is like’ has been elaborated. Now He elaborates the earlier promises ‘what its modifications are and from what it arises, and who the knower is and what his powers are’ by explaining how prakṛti and puruṣa cause saṃsāra, in five verses beginning ‘Prakṛti.’ If prakṛti and puruṣa had beginnings, another prakṛti would have to account for them, producing infinite regress. Therefore know both to be beginningless. Prakṛti is beginningless because it is the power of the beginningless Lord; puruṣa is beginningless because it is a portion of Him. The beginninglessness and eternality of the Supreme Lord and His powers have been established at great length by Śrī Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda in his Bhāṣya, so we do not expand it here. Know the modifications such as body and senses, and the guṇas—that is, transformations such as pleasure, pain and delusion—to arise from prakṛti.

विकाराणां प्रकृतिसंभवत्वं दर्शयन्पुरुषस्य संसारहेतुत्वं दर्शयति -- कार्यकारणेति। कार्यं शरीरम्? कारणानि सुखदुःखसाधनानीन्द्रियाणि? तेषां कर्तृत्वे तदाकारपरिणामे प्रकृतिर्हेतुरुच्यते कपिलादिभिः। पुरुषो जीवस्तत्कृतसुखदुःखानां भोक्तृत्वे हेतुरुच्यते। अयं भावःयद्यप्यचेतनायाः प्रकृतेः स्वतः कर्तृत्वं न संभवति? तथा पुरुषस्याप्यविकारिणो भोक्तृत्वं न संभवति? तथापि कर्तृत्वं नाम क्रियानिर्वर्तकत्वम् तच्चाचेतनस्यापि चेतनादृष्टवशाच्चैतन्याधिष्ठितत्वात्संभवति। यथा वह्नेरूर्ध्वज्वलनम्? वायोस्तिर्यग्गमनम्? वत्सादृष्टवशात्स्तन्यपयसः क्षरणमित्यादि। अतः पुरुषसंनिधानात्प्रकृतेः कर्तृत्वमुच्यते। भोक्तृत्वं च सुखदुःखसंवेदनम्। तच्चेतनधर्म एवेति संनिधानात्पुरुषस्य भोक्तृत्वमुच्यत इति।

Having shown that modifications arise from prakṛti, He shows how puruṣa causes saṃsāra. ‘Effect’ is the body; ‘instruments’ are the senses that produce pleasure and pain. Kapila and others say prakṛti is the cause of their agency, meaning their transformation into those forms. Puruṣa, the individual self, is said to be the cause of experiencing the pleasure and pain produced through them. The purport is this: although insentient prakṛti cannot be an agent independently, and immutable puruṣa cannot independently be an experiencer, ‘agency’ means bringing about an action; this can belong even to something insentient when presided over by consciousness under the force of the unseen, just as fire burns upward, wind moves sideways, or milk flows from a cow’s udder because of the calf’s unseen merit. Thus prakṛti is called agent because of the presence of puruṣa. Experience means awareness of pleasure and pain; because that belongs to consciousness, puruṣa is called experiencer by association.

तथाप्यविकारिणो जन्मरहितस्य भोक्तृत्वं कथमित्यत आह -- पुरुष इति। हि यस्मात्प्रकृतिस्थः तत्कार्यदेहे तादात्म्येन स्थितः पुरुषः। अतस्तज्जनितान्सुखादीन्भुङ्क्ते। अस्य च पुरुषस्य सतीषु देवादियोनिषु? असतीषु तिर्यगादियोनिषु यानि जन्मानि तेषु गुणसङ्गः। गुणैः शुभाशुभकर्मकारिभिरिन्द्रियैः सङ्गः कारणमित्यर्थः।

Still, how can the immutable, unborn puruṣa be an experiencer? Because puruṣa is ‘situated in prakṛti,’ identified with its product, the body, it experiences pleasure and the rest produced by it. The cause of this puruṣa’s births in good wombs such as divine births and bad wombs such as animal births is attachment to the guṇas—that is, attachment to the senses which perform good and evil actions under the guṇas.

तदनेन प्रकारेण प्रकृत्यविवेकात्पुरुषस्य संसारो न तु स्वरूपत इत्याशयेन तस्य स्वरूपमाह -- उपद्रष्टेति। अस्मिन्प्रकृतिकार्ये देहे च वर्तमानोऽपि पुरुषः परो भिन्न एव न तद्गुणैर्युज्यत इत्यर्थः। तत्र हेतवः -- यस्मादुपद्रष्टा पृथग्भूत एवं समीपे स्थित्वा द्रष्टा? तथाऽनुमन्ता अनुमोदितैव संनिधिमात्रेणानुग्राहकःसाक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च इत्यादिश्रुतेः। तथा ऐश्वरेण रूपेण भर्ता विधारक इति चोक्तः? भोक्ता पालक इति च? महांश्चासावीश्वरश्चेति? स ब्रह्मादीनामधिपतिरिति च? परमात्मान्तर्यामीति चोक्तः श्रुत्या। तथाच श्रुतिःएष भूताधिपतिरेष लोकेश्वर एष लोकपालः इत्यादिः।

Thus saṃsāra belongs to puruṣa because of non-discrimination from prakṛti, not by its own nature. With this intention He states puruṣa’s true nature. Even while present in this body, a product of prakṛti, puruṣa remains ‘other,’ distinct and not joined to its qualities. The reasons are that it is the witness who stands apart yet nearby and sees; the permitter who merely approves and bestows favor through presence, as scripture says ‘the witness, the conscious one, alone, without guṇas.’ In its lordly form it is called the supporter and sustainer, the enjoyer in the sense of protector, the great Lord, ruler of Brahmā and others, and the Supreme Self, inner controller. Scripture says, ‘This is the lord of beings, this is the lord of the world, this is the guardian of the world,’ and so on.

एवं प्रकृतिपुरुषविवेकज्ञानिनं स्तौति -- य एवमिति। एवमुपद्रष्टृत्वादिरुपेण पुरुषं यो वेत्ति? प्रकृतिं च गुणैः सुखदुःखादिपरिणामैः सहितां यो वेत्ति? स पुरुषः सर्वथा विधिमतिलङ्घ्य वर्तमानोऽपि पुनर्नाभिजायते। मुच्यत एवेत्यर्थः।

He praises one who knows the distinction between prakṛti and puruṣa. Whoever knows puruṣa in this way as witness and so forth, and knows prakṛti together with the guṇas and their transformations such as pleasure and pain, is not born again, even if in some way he lives having transgressed ordinary injunctions. The meaning is that he is certainly liberated.

एवंभूतविविक्तात्मज्ञाने साधनविकल्पानाह -- ध्यानेनेति द्वाभ्याम्। ध्यानेन आत्माकारप्रत्ययावृत्त्या। आत्मनि देहे आत्मना मनसा एवमात्मानं केचित्पश्यन्ति। अन्ये तु सांख्येन प्रकृतिपुरुषवैलक्षण्यालोचनेन? योगेनाष्टाङ्गेन? अपरे च कर्मयोगेन पश्यन्तीति सर्वत्रानुषङ्गः। एतेषां च ध्यानादीनां यथायोगं क्रमसमुच्चये सत्यपि तत्तन्निष्ठाभेदाभिप्रायेण विकल्पोक्तिः।

He offers alternative means for realizing the Self as distinct in this way, in two verses beginning ‘By meditation.’ By meditation means repeated mental cognition in the form of the Self; some see the Self in the body by the mind itself in this manner. Others see through Sāṃkhya, contemplation of the difference between prakṛti and puruṣa; others through eightfold yoga; still others through karma-yoga. ‘See’ is understood with each. Although meditation and these other means may appropriately occur in sequence and combination, alternatives are stated because different people are established primarily in different methods.

अतिमन्दाधिकारिणां निस्तारोपायमाह -- अन्य इति। अन्ये तु सांख्ययोगादिमार्गेणैवंभूतमुपद्रष्टृत्वादिलक्षणमात्मानं साक्षात्कर्तुमजानन्तोऽन्येभ्य आचार्येभ्य उपदेशेन श्रुत्वा उपासते ध्यायन्ति। ते च श्रद्धयोपदेशश्रवणपरायणाः सन्तो मृत्युं,संसारं शनैरतितरन्त्येव।

For those of very weak qualification He gives a means of deliverance. Others, unable to realize directly through Sāṃkhya, yoga and the other paths the Self characterized as witness and so forth, hear instruction from teachers and then worship and meditate. Devoted with faith to hearing that instruction, they too gradually cross death and saṃsāra.

तत्र कर्मयोगस्य तृतीयचतुर्थपञ्चमेषु प्रपञ्चितत्वात्? ध्यानयोगस्य च षष्ठाष्टमयोः प्रपञ्चितत्वात्? ध्यानादेश्च सांख्यविविक्तात्मविषयत्वात्सांख्यमेव प्रपञ्चयन्नाह -- यावदित्यादि। यावदध्यायसमाप्ति। यावत्किंचिद्वस्तुमात्रं सत्त्वमुत्पद्यते तत्सर्वं क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्योगात् अविवेककृतात्तादात्म्याध्यासाद्भवतीति जानीहि।

Since karma-yoga was elaborated in chapters three, four and five, meditation-yoga in chapters six and eight, and meditation itself has as its object the Self distinguished through Sāṃkhya, He now elaborates Sāṃkhya from ‘Whatever’ to the end of the chapter. Know that whatever entity whatsoever arises does so from the conjunction of field and knower of the field—that is, from superimposed identity produced by non-discrimination.

अविवेककृतं संसारोद्भवमुक्त्वा तन्निवृत्तये विविक्तात्मविषयं सम्यग्दर्शनमाह -- सममिति। स्थावरजङ्गमात्मकेषु भूतेषु निर्विशेषं सद्रूपेण समं यथा भवत्येवं तिष्ठन्तं परमात्मानं यः पश्यति? अतएव तेषु विनश्यत्स्वप्यविनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स एव सम्यवपश्यति नान्यः।

Having said that saṃsāra arises through non-discrimination, He teaches right vision of the distinct Self for its cessation. One who sees the Supreme Self abiding equally, without distinction, as pure Being in all stationary and moving beings, and therefore sees It as imperishable even when they perish, alone sees rightly; no one else does.

कुत इत्यत आह -- सममिति। सर्वत्र भूतमात्रे समं सम्यगप्रच्युतस्वरूपेणावस्थितं परमात्मानं पश्यन् हि यस्मादात्मना स्वेनैवात्मानं न हिनस्ति अविद्यया सच्चिदानन्दरूपमात्मानं तिरस्कृत्य न विनाशयति। ततश्च परां गतिं मोक्षमाप्नोति। यस्त्वेवं न पश्यति स हि देहात्मदर्शी देहेन सहात्मानं हिनस्ति। तथाच श्रुतिः -- असुर्या नाम ते लोका अन्धेन तमसावृताः। तांस्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छन्त्येके चात्महनो जनाः इति।

Why? Seeing the Supreme Self everywhere in all beings, equally and in its unfailing true nature, one does not injure the Self by the self—that is, one does not destroy awareness of the Self of the nature of being, consciousness and bliss by covering it through ignorance. Therefore one attains the supreme goal, liberation. One who does not see thus identifies the self with the body and destroys it along with the body. Scripture says, ‘Those worlds are demonic, covered by blind darkness; after death those people who are slayers of the Self enter them.’

ननु शुभाशुभकर्मकर्तृत्वेन वैषम्ये दृश्यमाने कथमात्मनः समत्वमित्याशङ्क्याह -- प्रकृत्यैवेति। प्रकृत्यैव देहेन्द्रियाकारेण परिणतया सर्वशः सर्वैः प्रकारैः क्रियमाणानि कर्माणि यः पश्यति? तथात्मानं? चाकर्तारं देहाभिमानेनैवात्मनः कर्तृत्वं न स्वतः इत्येवं यः पश्यति? स एव सम्यक्पश्यति नान्य इत्यर्थः।

But when difference is seen through the performance of good and evil actions, how can the Self be equal? He answers: one who sees all actions as performed in every way by prakṛti alone, transformed into body and senses, and sees the Self as non-agent—its apparent agency arising only from identification with the body and not from its own nature—alone sees rightly.

इदानी तु भूतानां प्रकृतितावन्मात्रत्वेनाभेदाद्भूतभेदकृतमप्यात्मनो भेदमपश्यन्ब्रह्मत्वमुपैतीत्याह -- यदेति। यदा भूतानां स्थावरजङ्गमानां पृथग्भावं भेदं पृथक्त्वं एकस्थं एकस्यामेवेश्वरशक्तिरूपायां प्रकृतौ स्थितं प्रलयेऽनुपश्यत्यालोचयति? तत एव च तस्या एव प्रकृतेः सकाशाद्भूतानां विस्तारं सृष्टिसमयेऽनुपश्यति? तदा प्रकृतितावन्मात्रत्वेन भूतानामप्यभेदं पश्यन्परिपूर्णं ब्रह्म संपद्यते। ब्रह्मैव भवतीत्यर्थः।

Now He says that because beings are nothing but prakṛti, one who no longer sees difference in the Self caused by differences among beings attains Brahman. When one sees that the separateness and distinctions of stationary and moving beings rest in one thing alone, prakṛti as the Lord’s power, at dissolution, and sees their expansion at creation arise from that same prakṛti, then seeing beings as non-different insofar as they are merely prakṛti, one attains complete Brahman—that is, becomes Brahman itself.

तथापि परमेश्वरस्य संसारावस्थायां देहकर्मसंबन्धनिमित्तैः कर्मभिस्तत्फलैश्च सुखदुःखादिवैषम्यं दुष्परिहरमिति कुतः समदर्शनं तत्राह -- अनादित्वादिति। यदुत्पत्तिमत्तदेव हि व्येति विनाशमेति। यच्च गुणवद्वस्तु तस्य गुणनाशे व्ययो भवति। अयं तु परमात्मा अनादिर्निर्गुणश्चातोऽव्ययः। अविकारीत्यर्थः। तस्माच्छरीरे स्थितोऽपि किंचिन्न करोति? नच कर्मफलैर्लिप्यत इति।

Still, in the state of saṃsāra, because of relation to body and action, inequality through actions and their fruits such as pleasure and pain seems unavoidable for the Supreme Self; how then equal vision? Whatever has an origin perishes, and whatever possesses qualities perishes when those qualities are destroyed. But the Supreme Self is beginningless and without guṇas, therefore imperishable—meaning changeless. Hence, though situated in the body, It does nothing and is not tainted by karmic fruits.

तत्र दृष्टान्तमाह -- यथेति। यथा सर्वत्र पङ्कादिष्वपि स्थितमाकाशं सौक्ष्यादसङ्गत्वात्पङ्कादिभिर्नोपलिप्यते तथा सर्वत्र उत्तमे मध्यमेऽधमे वा देहेऽवस्थितोऽप्यात्मा नोपलिप्यते। दैहिकैर्गुणदोषैर्न युज्यत इत्यर्थः।

He gives an example: just as space, though present everywhere even in mud and the like, is not stained by mud because of its subtlety and non-attachment, so the Self, though present everywhere in high, middle or low bodies, is not stained; it does not become connected with bodily merits and defects.
असङ्गत्वाल्लेपो नास्तीत्याकाशदृष्टान्तेनोक्तम्? प्रकाशकत्वाच्च प्रकाश्यधर्मैर्न युज्यत इति रविदृष्टान्तेनाह -- यथेति। स्पष्टार्थः।

The example of space showed that there is no stain because of non-attachment. Now, by the example of the sun, He shows that because the Self is the illuminator it is not connected with the properties of what it illuminates. The meaning is clear.
